item.title: Games industry analysts told IGN that BioWare was likely doomed well before EA’s $55 billion acquisition, explaining that games like Mass Effect are now considered “prestige projects” for the company, and it’s unlikely the sci-fi franchise, nor BioWare’s other IPs, are sold off.
item.description:
Games industry analysts told IGN that BioWare was likely doomed well before EA’s $55 billion acquisition, explaining that games like Mass Effect are now considered “prestige projects” for the company, and it’s unlikely the sci-fi franchise, nor BioWare’s other IPs, are sold off.
On October 21, EA announced a major shift in strategy and a significant internal restructuring that involves the cancelation of a number of projects, the closure of BioWare, and a reported 400 people losing their jobs. The Canadian studio, known for franchises like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, was shut down after more than 30 years of creating beloved role-playing games. Mass Effect fans must now consider that the franchise is dead — something the leaked internal trailer for Mass Effect Universe made all the more difficult to accept.
Needless to say, Mass Effect fans were gutted by the news, hoping against hope that EA might sell off BioWare’s IP rather than letting them languish in obscurity. But analysts have expressed doubt that outside companies will take on BioWare's franchises, even as EA faces down a massive debt incurred by its acquisition.
When asked about this possibility, industry analyst Joost van Dreunen said, “maybe,” but explained that these IPs are likely far too costly — and far too time-consuming — for other developers to tackle.
“In many ways, BioWare's IP is in the same boat as some of the other studios we recently saw being divested. They are all well-known and too expensive for most buyers. Capable publishers like CD Projekt Red already have their hands full with their own projects,” he said. (He’s not wrong; CDPR certainly has a lot on its plate right now, what with The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 being in active development.)
The next Mass Effect was announced six years ago, at The Game Awards 2020, and this time last year Mike Gamble, now former executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, celebrated N7 Day to say the game was still in development. He even expressed excitement about the Amazon TV series (which IGN understands is currently still in the works), and insisted EA and BioWare "remain committed to telling more stories in this universe."
So what changed? Why cancel Mass Effect 5 now? Van Dreunen told us that, in EA’s eyes, legacy IPs like Mass Effect are likely being viewed as “prestige projects,” and the future looks grim for other development teams still underneath EA’s umbrella.
"Before its buyout, EA had been focusing on building recurring revenue streams, and the focus of its new owners is sports, live service, and new markets like Asia. Even if Mass Effect and Dragon Age were fantastically successful, corporate will insist on predictable cash flow. It makes franchises like Mass Effect a prestige project,” he continued.
“Considering the debt load, I'd expect to hear about more layoffs in the months to come. The memo already shrinks the skate. team and pauses a project for The Sims. I expect EA's town hall in November to bring more bad news."
Van Dreunen, along with fellow analyst Piers Harding-Rolls of Ampere, considers BioWare’s closure an inevitable consequence of EA’s current business structure, calling it “entirely predictable and precisely what a leveraged buyout looks like once the deal closes.
“In this case, EA now carries roughly $18 billion in debt, which costs it about $1.8 billion a year in interest. That is more than its annual EBITDA of around $1.5 billion. EA has told its lenders it will cut $700 million in annual costs to service the debt. In that context, a 50-person team working on a game that is years from launch is the easiest line to cut, regardless of its legacy,” van Dreunen said.
“This news is emotive for many adult gamers because of Bioware’s long history of delivering games with deep narratives that connect with audiences, meaning it has a large cultural footprint. It’s a name that has been around for 30 years, so seeing it close is a significant moment for the industry. In particular, the original Baldur’s Gate games, Neverwinter Nights, and KOTOR were genre defining, and the later Mass Effect titles also strongly resonated with audiences,” Harding-Rolls told us.
Harding-Rolls added that the commercial failure of BioWare's last game, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, played a part in BioWare's demise. And let's remember that 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda and 2019's Anthem also failed to meet EA's expectations.
“Unfortunately, the studio’s recent big-budget releases have not performed well enough commercially," he said. "Ampere data shows that Bioware’s latest release at the end of 2024 — Dragon Age: The Veilguard — has sold an estimated 1.9 million units globally across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam up to the end of September, way below internal targets. The changing nature of high-end gaming and the need to cut costs means that it is likely that Bioware’s future was under discussion before EA was acquired by the PIF and its partners.”
It's a point backed up by MST Financial analyst David Gibson. “I think the closing is a combination of factors: EA going private and needing to improve returns and margins to fund large debt, high relative costs in the West (versus Asia, etc.) to develop AAA games, and role playing games like Mass Effect not doing enough sales to be profitable enough,” he explained.
“It appears there were many other games in development using IP which were also scrapped. I would hope a small and nimble studio would acquire some of the IP and make great games that users love and that contain innovation, rather than repeat the same stuff. EA has a history of making a series of games that are just not fun to play or contain innovation.”
Whether or not EA ends up selling off BioWare’s IP remains to be seen. Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah is more optimistic about this possibility than he was previously, but remains skeptical, saying EA could be just as likely to “forget they ever existed and bury them in the vault.”
We have much more on the dramatic news of BioWare's closure, including reaction from fans and the video game industry, and IGN's Ryan McCaffrey on why BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: The developers of Mass Effect-style game Exodus picked a hell of a time to reveal their redesigned male protagonist.
item.description:
Archetype has shown off its updated character model for the male version of Exodus protagonist Jun Aslan. Prior to this, fans had complained about Jun’s “long” face, “beady eyes,” and “botox” cheeks.
“He just looks uncannily plastic surgery filled who's constantly serving his best iPhone face,” said one person at the time. “He looks like chad version of Timothee Chalamet (derogatory),” said another.
With his makeover complete, Jun has gone full twink mode, and looks a bit like Leon Kennedy’s younger brother. The rough edges have been sanded down and now he looks like he could front a space boy band. Dem cheekbones.
Fans on Reddit seem much happier. “Not a huge fan of the default hair TBH but I can change that so all's good — the facial structure has really improved,” said one poster. “OHHHHH that is so much better. He looks like a dashing space hero instead of a bad go in the character creator, which is perfect,” said another.
The timing of this new trailer is interesting. Players are looking at Exodus and Owlcat's The Expanse: Osiris Reborn as spiritual successors to the dormant Mass Effect series. Exodus is clearly inspired by Mass Effect, putting you in the shoes of a ship captain making tough choices across alien worlds. It also puts an emphasis on relationships with your crew, who you can bump uglies with. Indeed, former Mass Effect developers, such as lead writer Drew Karpyshyn, are working on the game.
With EA announcing Mass Effect developer BioWare’s closure and the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 this week, this Exodus announcement feels like a timely reminder that space RPGs are still very much on the menu, and BioWare lives on in spirit at other studios.
Exodus fans have picked up on this, too, with some pointing to the Jun reveal coming hot on the heels of the leaked Mass Effect 5 trailer, which suggested a Mass Effect Universe title for the canceled game. "Who is here after watching the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer?" one Exodus fan said. "I purposely watched the Universe trailer first and Exodus last so I'd feel a little better," another said.
"Great timing Archetype!!!" one person commented. "This couldn’t have been revealed at a better time with the fallout of BioWare’s closure. The cheekbones really were the issue I think and this new, younger looking model really addresses it plainly and completely. Hopefully this satisfies the complainers who have made such a rabble about Jun’s face!"
When you play Jun Aslan, you choose whether they are male or female, with options like hairstyles, hair color, facial hair, and tattoos available to the player. Archetype has yet to reveal 'FemJun,' but did promise we'll see her soon. "We’ve got something special cooking for her reveal, and we think it’ll be worth the wait," Archetype teased.
Archetype promises a dark story where your actions have a massive impact on the world around you, with branching dialog trees where your choices matter. A butterfly flaps its wings on one planet, and a bit of space dust sticks in a dude’s eye lightyears away. Exodus is planned for launch on April 7, 2027, for PS5, Xbox Series X and S, and PC.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Infinity Ward's Multiplayer boss weighs in on Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 matchmaking.
item.description:
The Call of Duty matchmaking debate has raged on pretty much since the beginning of multiplayer. Should matches be comprised of evenly skilled players, if there’s an accurate enough way of ensuring that? Or should skill be stripped out of the equation, so you never know what to expect from the next match?
Both sides of the argument have their valid reasons for their preference, but most recently, in 2025’s Black Ops 7, an option was presented that attempted to satisfy all. While the default matchmaking was set to skill-based, as has been the case since 2007’s game-changing Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, open matchmaking playlists were also available to those who want the opportunity to get teamed up with, and against, anybody.
This year’s Modern Warfare 4, though, has launched without that option, once again placing the matchmaking debate into the spotlight within the COD community. Is there any way to keep everyone happy, then? IGN spoke with Infinity Ward's Multiplayer creative director, Joe Cecot, who explained that match quality is the priority.
“I don't know if there's perfecting it,” Cecot said of matchmaking. “For us, I think the most important thing when we look at matchmaking is that the matches we put together are good matches. And we're also looking at the players and their experience, and we can look at the data and how it affects things, and we can quantify how it affects a certain group of players or a large percentage of them in a negative way. And so, though we're not talking about exact specifics on matchmaking, our end goal is that every match is a good match.”
A fairly vague answer, then, and one befitting of the often-shrouded way that skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) works behind the scenes of Call of Duty matches. As previously noted, SBMM has been part of COD since the original Modern Warfare, but players only really started to feel it affecting their online experience once the algorithms were tightened from the 2019 reboot onwards.
On the surface, SBMM seems like a logical thing to want to employ in an online shooter — evenly skilled players being pitted against each other should make for the most exciting, closely contested matches. But the problem comes when you start overachieving and play out of your skin for a couple of rounds, with the algorithm then reacting and placing you in a much higher skill-level match next time up, only for you to have a miserable time getting your head popped off every time you peek around a corner. In theory, it’s a smart system, but in reality, it can lead to whiplash from one match to the next.
Is there any way to perfect it? Perhaps not. But Black Ops 7’s open queue did at least give players the option to roll the dice and opt out of skill-based matchmaking and join open queues if they wanted to. There’s a spot of confusion among the playerbase as to whether this is included in MW4, though — a persistent lobby option is available within the popular modes tab, but it doesn’t state whether this means open matchmaking is in effect. The fact that open matchmaking seemingly isn’t in MW4 at launch, or at the very least isn’t clearly displayed as being present, is therefore a little baffling.
For more on Modern Warfare 4, you can check out our review of the campaign, which will soon have multiplayer impressions added, or what we think of the extraction shooter mode, DMZ, so far.
We’ve got an in-progress Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Walkthrough to help you through the campaign missions, plus All Collectible Note Locations, and all the Code Solutions you’ll need to open every keypad and container. For multiplayer, check out How to Level Up Fast in MW4 and our Essential Multiplayer Tips and Tricks alongside the Best MW4 Settings we recommend you use. DMZ is back, so we’ve got a handy DMZ Beginner’s Guide, too.
Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social.

Since its debut in 2023, Disney Lorcana Trading Card Game by Ravensburger has sold over 2.8 billion cards inspired by some of the biggest films in Disney and Pixar's catalog, all while cultivating a thriving community of players that collect, battle, and dream of what's ahead. Today, on the official launch day of the Hyperia City set, we wanted to share our chat with Disney Lorcana TCG co-founder Ryan Miller from D23 as we got an exciting glimpse of the game's future.
The team held a panel at D23 called The Quests Ahead for Disney Lorcana Trading Card Game and we learned a lot of exciting details about what's headed our way this year and beyond, but what I'll remember most about our conversation was how this TCG has become so much more than just a game, but we'll get to that in a bit!
For now, let's break down all the big news!
The Hyperia City set is out now and has brought the world of Coco into Disney Lorcana TCG, added a new energy source called Ink Drops, and so much more. The title of this set is also kind of a big deal because the team has created a bustling urban landscape that builds out the game's lore in a fresh way.
"We have novelists, visual developers, and storytellers who just keep leveling up, and I think Hyperia City is a great example of that," Miller said. "It starts with a simple question, what would an urban environment in the realm of Lorcana look like? What would that be like? And then we had them go in and play around in that idea and it was really exciting all around."
A fun nod the team came up with was in the name itself, as it stems from Hyperion Studio, where Walt Disney Studios called home from 1926-1940 and where Mickey Mouse was born. From there, they had fun dividing the city into "distinct neighborhoods celebrating the individual attributes of various Illumineers and glimmers" that call it home.
This idea was then an inspiration for new location cards, so you'll be learning about the city while you play/collect. These include Land of the Dead – Marigold Bridge, Merlin’s Shop and Smithy – Magical Market, Khan Industries – Greenway Landmark, Institute of Technology – Honey Lemon’s Lab, and Khan Stadium – State of the Art.
And of course the locations need to be filled with glimmers, and we were introduced to Minnie Mouse - Urban Visionary, Donald Duck - Taxi Driver, and Mickey Mouse - Best in Town. These glimmers fit the theme of Hyperia City so well and show how the team is smartly integrating beloved characters to fit the set. Oh, and we have to mention that Mickey's card is a tribute to the first words he ever spoke: Hot Dog!
We had the chance to get an early hands-on of Hyperia City, and here's what we said;
"Hyperia City brings familiarity in returning characters, another popular Pixar addition, and a game-changing mechanic in ink drops to end the year," IGN's Mike Mamon wrote. "Characters from Big Hero 6 and The Sword of the Stone are back in a big way, which is a nice touch after the big set rotation, making some of their older cards unusable in the main competitive scene.
"Plus, with another Pixar favorite in Coco being highlighted, the set is very enticing for players and collectors out there. And with ink drops being a pretty major mechanic introduction adding another layer of resource management, it’ll be interesting to see how the meta and deck brewing changes as the competitive season progresses."
We also learned more about 2027's Into the Inkdark set, which will feature villains like Hades and task players with discovering the Dark Illuminary.
Perhaps the biggest news from this set, however, is that it will be introducing the Collector Boosters. These packs are meant for the collectors out there, as they include 12 randomized premium foil cards, each with a special foil treatment.
There will also be a new rarity - Illustrious - and we got a look at one of them - Maleficent - Biding Her Time - and learned it will be just one of six cards per set, and only 23 of each will be printed. And yes, Miller did confirm that they chose 23 as a nod to the founding year of The Walt Disney Company - 1923!
Miller also eased fears and assured me that this wouldn't change anything about booster packs or how players currently engage with the game.
"The Collector Booster is our way of saying to our collectors that this is a wonderful thing you can be excited about. It you want to really bling out your deck, this is a really good way to do that," Miller said. "It's not going to replace regular boosters. We really want this to just be a special thing that also focuses on the artists, which are featured right above the rarity symbol. We've worked with over 300 artists from around the world, and they are all truly amazing."
These Collector Boosters will be part of every set following Into the Inkdark, and they'll only be available for purchase at Ravensburger Play Hub stores, the Ravensburger Online Store, and select Disney locations.
Disney Lorcana TCG is going to space later in 2027 with the Cosmic Quest set, and we got a glimpse of what to expect with some fun art featuring The Little Mermaid's Ariel and Flounder floating among the cosmos.
I asked Miller what this new biome offers the team, and he said it's another evolution of what they did with Hyperia City in trying to explore new ideas and give the fans something they didn't even know they wanted.
"Narrative and game design, they work really closely together because they're really symbiotic," Miller said. "The game designers say, 'Well, we need these mechanics in the game. How can we best be expressed through story?' And then narratives say, 'Well, we're having a story with a setting, like this galactic setting, how can that fit the gameplay?' From that, they've done some really fun stuff there that I won't be sharing with you quite yet!"
What's the most exciting part for me about Cosmic Quest is that, for the very first time, Wall-E and EVE will be joining Disney Lorcana TCG with Cosmic Quest!
Of all the big reveals at D23, I think I was most blown away by the Beauty and the Beast Curator's Collection set. Listen, it's no secret that the art of Disney Lorcana TCG is on another level thanks to some truly incredible artists, and this set is the perfect example of how the team keeps one upping themselves.
This Curator's Collection set, which is the second one following the Heroines Edition, will be released in October 2026 and is part of the celebration of The Beauty and the Beast's 30th anniversary. What sets this collection apart is that the artwork takes inspiration from the movie's stained-glass motif, and these cards are gorgeous. The character art in concert with the colors come together so beautifully, and there is also just so much joy in each of the faces. I know this will be hard to get, but this feels like a must have!
"To me it's a love letter," Miller said of this set. "It's our love letter to our fans, and it's our love letter to Beauty and the Beast. Furthermore, the attention to detail is how we show our love. It's something that Disney exemplifies, and they're the best in the world at this, and that attention to detail is how we show our love for these characters and stories on those cards. You've only seen the video of it, but to hold them in your hands and to see what actually went into these, it's amazing. Our creative team is second to none. They make such beautiful cards."
Speaking of Disney Lorcana TCG's artwork, the Disney Lorcana Visual Guide is on its way to store shelves on February 1, 2027, and is meant for fans who want to dive deep into the lore and/or just admire a collection of art in a coffee style book you can display with pride. This book gathers art from many of the different sets and scales them up so they can be appreciated even more, and I'm all for that!
If D23 showed us anything, it's that Figment is, deservedly, having quite a moment! In addition to the news that Figment and Dreamfinder will be part of a new iteration of Journey Into Imagination at EPCOT, the team at Disney Lorcana TCG confirmed they will be back at EPCOT's International Festival of the Arts with the first-ever Figment card!
Miller shared that over 170,000 people participated in the first collection quest at the last festival, and Figment spearheading the next one just feels right.
"It's just wonderful," Miller said of finally getting Figment on a card. "At the last festival, they had a Figment popcorn bucket and there was this huge line. It's just so great when a character just brings people together. So, to be able to include Figment on a Lorcana card is just so cool. I also think we found the perfect card for him, and I was really excited to hear the crowd when we revealed it.
"I don't know how else to put it, but Disney fans are so delightful. This Figment love is just so neat to me, I mean, he's not been in a film, but they love him. One of the favorite things about my job is I love, love, love when people are geeking out about stuff they love. And I say this as a lifelong geek, right? I love it. It's wonderful. My eye doctor was geeking out about the veins in my eye and I'm like, 'keep going!' He's like, 'I'm probably boring.' I'm like, 'No, dude, it's super compelling.'"
To conclude Disney Lorcana TCG's panel at D23, the team shared they are hard at work on a digital version of the game. The goal is to allow players to play how they want, when they want, and where they want in a simpler way.
"For me, there are two main things," Miller said of the digital version. "One is that this is for Lorcana players who, for whatever reason, have a lifestyle change or something like that. If they have a toddler, for example, and can't go to their weeklies as much as they want to, this is for them. Or maybe they haven't found their weeklies yet or just want to practice, this will be an incredible tool for that.
"On the other hand, it's an invaluable tool for learning how to play. A lot of us, myself included, might feel a bit of a social cost when we're being taught by someone. We're like, 'Oh, what did you say again?' Or, 'I don't want to bug you, you're the middle of teaching me, blah, blah, blah.' And the digital game is such a great way to do that; to just learn in a social free environment. I could just learn there and then build up my confidence and my skill level so that I can then feel more empowered to go to a weekly, to go to an event, to simply sit down with somebody and play. Sitting down on the tabletop is so fun, and we're hoping this helps more people get there."
Those voyaging on Disney Cruise Line in 2027 will also have a chance to experience Disney Lorcana TCG as Collection Quests and more will join the fleet, meaning there are even more ways to play!
Disney Lorcana TCG had a huge presence at D23, and Miller shared that this convention will always have a special place in the team's heart as the 2022 show is where the game was revealed to the world.
"Before that moment at D23 2022, we just weren't sure," Miller said. "We had a booth that was probably a 10th of the size of the one we have now, and we just weren't sure. And then the crowd showed up and we had a huge line. It was this wonderful moment for us and it gave a much needed boost, because we'd been working on this project for nearly two years in the dark."
At D23 this year, Disney Lorcana TCG and Ravensburger as a whole had photo ops, a collection quest, a D23 Challenge Championship Qualifier, and, of course, some exclusive, current, and pre-release items for the army of fans to enjoy.
The big ticket item was the 2026 D23 Collection, which included beloved glimmers from past quests and, perhaps most exciting, the first-ever card from the upcoming Hyperia set - Coco's Héctor Rivera. The set also includes Lilo & Stitch's Angel, Pocahontas, Mulan's Mushu, Zootopia's Judy Hopps, and The Incredibles' Mr. Incredible.
As a huge fan of Winnie the Pooh (Happy 100th BTW!), the highlight for me just may have been the Winnie the Pooh - Hunny Wizard Premium Playmat. This gorgeous playmat features premium hunny foil details and stitched edges, and just looks so good in person.
A much-anticipated pre-release item at D23 was the Quest of Wonders: An Illumineers Lorebook. This first-of-its-kind novel not only features incredible art from Disney Lorcana TCG's artists an a stunning Pegasus promo card, but actualy tells a story from inside the game's world.
The story follows Illumineer Shanzay, who comes across an old lorebook and is trying to figure out who it belonged to and why it was hidden.
"The more she reads about the author's adventure—how he set out with his glimmers of Peter Pan and Pegasus in search of his missing mentor—the more shocking her discoveries become, which she records in margin notes," the official description reads.
Such other exciting items on display were some of the Lorcana puzzles, and I was so excited to put together the Winnie the Pooh & Piglet - Hunny Mages 300-piece puzzle with my son as it paired perfectly with the playmat!
There was also the Disney Lorcana TCG: Collection Starter Set - Rapunzel Edition, which comes with 4 random packs, a Collector's Card Portfolio with Rapunzel herself, a Collector's Guide, and a stunning spcial edition promo card of Rapunzel - Ethereal Protector.
Oh, and Disney Villainous is still going strong at Ravensburger, and we were able to get our hands on the Come, We Fly! expansion that celebrates Hocus Pocus' Sanderson Sisters and even comes with an exclusive game piece of the sisters that will be sure to be a treat to any fan of the film.
To end our conversation, Miller and I just spoke for a few moments about what Disney Lorcana TCG really means to the players around the world. As with many of the things they love, they become so much more than what they appear on the surface because of the memories and moments we create with them with the ones we love.
"I'm just so proud to be a part of something that could make people this happy," Miller said with a big smile on his face. "I'm also just so proud of this team. They have done so many fantastic things in a short amount of time, and I'm really proud to be a part of that too. What we're doing here is special, and we're not here to squeeze the juice out of the grapes. We're here because we want to grow the vines. We want to grow more grapes. It's a long process, but it's really important."
And those vines have spread in ways the team could never have predicted, and I have one final story to share with you from Miller that sums it all up perfectly.
"There was a fellow I was talking to earlier today who was a special education teacher," Miller said. "He was at one of his locals when a kid came in with his parent who wasn't really engaging or anything like that, and he taught this kid how to play. Now, this kid has totally come out of his shell and has become a competitor and a really good player. This was his thing now. It was something that he could really own and it was his deal. And I just love that because who knows what else could happen? It's just wonderful when you send ripples out in the world and some of them come back. It's just a wonderful thing."
For more, check out all the other big reveals from D23's Entertainment and Experiences Showcases!

item.title: Cyberpunk 2077’s surprise 2.5 update added a new dual-wielding playstyle, fresh ways to customize protagonist V’s look, extra quests and plenty more, but players have discovered that developer CD Projekt Red secretly added a range of new The Witcher 3-themed cosmetics, too.
item.description:
Cyberpunk 2077’s surprise 2.5 update added a new dual-wielding playstyle, fresh ways to customize protagonist V’s look, extra quests and plenty more, but players have discovered that developer CD Projekt Red secretly added a range of new The Witcher 3-themed cosmetics, too.
The Cyberpunk 2077: Edgerunners update snuck in some sweet new clothes for V to wear, as well as the professor spectacles Geralt can wear in The Witcher 3.
As mentioned by @SynthPotato on X / Twitter, you can access the items at V’s apartment once you get a text from Arianne about a gift. It’s a similar method used for other drops added to the game.
@SynthPotato They also added this knife that you missed (similar one Geralt uses to collect trophies in TW3) https://t.co/aWH0XwerMS
None of this was included in the official Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 patch notes, which mostly focused on the Edgerunners crossover and a new questline featuring Night City founder Richard Night. Those new Glamdocs look nice though — I’ve always wanted to pimp my chrome and add some color to those gorilla arms.
The Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime just got its second season. Set after the events of the game, Edgerunners 2 features a cast of fresh characters as they navigate the dystopian hell of Night City’s corporation-ruled future. Game director Hideo Kojima made a cheeky cameo in it.
CDPR has also partnered with Paramount to make a live-action movie based on the game. However, the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won’t retrace the game’s steps. Smile 2 star Kyle Gallner said he would love to play V, though the news that it won’t follow the games could mean V doesn’t even exist in the movie.
CDPR had ruled out Cyberpunk 2077 DLC, so this 2.5 update came as a welcome surprise. Some fans still want a Cyberpunk 2077 expansion, though, and are encouraged by The Witcher 3's upcoming expansion, Songs of the Past, which arrives 12 years after the base game launched. Meanwhile, Cyberpunk 2 is in development, as is The Witcher 4 and a number of other games.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: X-Files creator Chris Carter on how his I Want to Believe Director's Cut dovetailed into his second feature, Queens for a Day.
item.description:
2026 has been an interesting year of independence and creativity for The X-Files creator Chris Carter. In August, Hulu released Carter’s Director’s Cut of his 2008 feature debut, The X-Files: I Want to Believe - Vrach Frankenshteyn, with the title and tone he always intended. And this month, he’s promoting the limited release of his second feature, the self-funded indie, Queens for a Day.
IGN attended a recent Santa Monica screening of the time-twisting, cautionary tale with a defiantly political message, Queens for a Day. Carter and the film’s screenwriter, wife Dori Carter, attracted a who’s who of former X-Files staffers including Darren Morgan, Glen Morgan, Annabeth Gish, Kristen Cloke, and Jeff Cahn.
After, Gish led a Q&A with Carter who confirmed that his 2025 recut of The X-Files: I Want to Believe - Vrach Frankenshteyn dovetailed into preproduction for Queen, and even shared several X-Files collaborators like editor Cahn and production designer Mark S. Freeborn. Specifically, Vrach Frankenshteyn locked in December 2025. In early 2026, Carter relocated to his old X-Files stomping ground in Vancouver, British Columbia where he filmed over a tight 32 days. He then edited with Cahn, locking the final cut around October 9 with the most timely political topics he was able to include.
In an exclusive IGN chat, the recently-turned-70 Carter said it’s been a big year for him creatively, and that he’s pleased that he finally got to revisit The X-Files: I Want to Believe which initially wasn’t received well by the fandom.
“I just felt like I had made a movie and they made me change it,” Carter said of his initial disappointment with Fox’s cuts. “I wanted to make the movie a scary movie. It was a Frankenstein movie. No one ever appreciated, or got to appreciate it as Frankenstein. I actually got to put the title Frankenstein in it, so that was very important to me. We made sure it’s an X-Files movie that draws on the Frankenstein story and that's what I tried to put back into it.”
Carter enthusiastically said he was happy with how his cut was received by critics and fans, though he acknowledges the Mulder/Scully shippers were not pleased with his cuts. “The relation-shippers were not happy that I took out some Mulder and Scully,” he said pragmatically. “But we also just did two [season] reboots and Scully learns that she is pregnant in the last one. So when I went back to do I Want to Believe, I had to keep that in mind, that if this is a movie I want people to watch now, that it doesn't feel dated.”
He explained in the Q&A that the Queen for a Day screenplay was written 30-years ago by Dori, optioned but never got greenlit. Recently, he discovered the screenplay in a box during some housecleaning, so he encouraged her to update her Twilight-Zone styled story about an adult daughter, estranged from her traditional mother. When she gets into a car crash, the daughter wakes up in her mother’s body in the 1950s and gets to live her life literally in her mother's shoes.
“I said to Dori, ‘I think you should do this in the political moment we're living in, and you should make the character a right-wing newscaster like Jeanine Pirro who was on [Fox New’s] The Five,’ Carter said. “And that’s really the genesis of the project.”
In its current iteration in Queen, the daughter is Judge Jerri, a big, brash conservative MAGA news pundit (played by actress Erin Boyes) who goes through a journey of begrudging empathy, coming to understanding her mother’s struggles as a single mother and more generally a disappointed woman in an era that afforded her few independent options. She comes to see where her bitterness has poisoned not only her world, but helped do so in the broader toxic political discourse.
Carter said the finished film scared all the studios and distributors but he’s still working on securing one. “The reason we wanted to do this was not just to tell a good tale, but to raise our fists. We’re angry we are living in a world we don't want to live in, and so this is our response to that. And I should say, this story owes to Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, where Scrooge gets to see the past and present and the future, and what Jerri sees is the future that changes her life.”
He also agreed that Rod Serling’s Twilight Zone was a big inspiration. “I just read something really interesting about Rod Serling, that he kept trying to write things that they wouldn't let him put on television,” Carter told IGN. “And he finally figured out for The Twilight Zone, if you write things allegorically, you can actually put things on film that you wouldn't be able to do.”

When it comes to board games, a frequent “Holy Grail” game (a term used to describe a game that someone has been hunting for, usually out of print and expensive) on many lists is Fantasy Flight Games’ Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game. But it looks like the search may be coming to an end for fans, as it was announced today that Ghost Galaxy has entered into an agreement with Universal and Fantasy Flight Games to publish a brand-new edition of this coveted title, coming to crowdfunding early next year.
First released back in 2008 and featuring imagery from the Sci-Fi Channel reboot, this social deduction/hidden traitor game wonderfully captured the tension from the show, where anyone could be a secret Cylon agent trying to thwart the single mission of the humans—to get home. Battlestar Galactica would go on to get three expansions, but almost a decade ago now, it all went out of print, and now prices on the secondary market for a full set (base game + expansions) could easily cost you more than a grand. Back in 2021, FFG did release a sort of reskinned version of BSG with Unfathomable, which replaced the Galactica with a boat and the Cylons with Lovecraftian horrors, which has seen success as well.
Details on this new edition are scant right now; all we have is that it’s a “new edition” that will feature “an updated design,” whatever that means, but I think the game is in safe hands. Overseeing this project will be Christian T. Peterson, the CEO of Ghost Galaxy and formerly the founder and CEO of Fantasy Flight Games and the creator of a little game called Twilight Imperium.
Recently, Fantasy Flight Games launched a similar campaign as the debut of its “Vault Series” with Arkham Horror Remastered (check out our interview and exclusive art reveal), which seeks to accomplish a similar goal with the much-loved Arkham Horror Second Edition. item.title: Cyberpunk 2 associate game director Pawel Sasko revealed that much of the game’s staff are actually former modders who CD Projekt Red picked up to work on the highly-anticipated sequel.
item.description:
Cyberpunk 2 associate game director Pawel Sasko revealed that a good chunk of the game’s staff are actually former modders who CD Projekt Red picked up to work on the highly-anticipated sequel.
Sasko made these comments during one of CDPR’s REDstreams on October 21, where the team discussed the bevy of exciting new updates coming to Cyberpunk 2077. As part of this discussion, they explained their decision to introduce cross-platform support for PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series X|S, saying this was done both to keep the game fresh and to actively support the creativity of its modders.
In fact, the good folks at CDPR have actually partnered with modders in the game’s community as part of these updates, and even credited them with helping keep the title afloat.
“The modding community is really keeping the game alive,” Sasko said. “I’m very often looking at what our modders are doing, what they’re building. It’s very exciting. There’s so much creativity. We as a studio always try to support our modding community as much as we can.”
Adding onto this discussion, Sasko revealed that CDPR has sourced quite a few of its staff working on Cyberpunk 2 from the game’s modding scene, saying that around half of its quest team — designers who create a game’s objectives and storyline segments — are former modders.
"A lot of modders, they were players who actually first played and actually got experience with customizing the game with the mods," he said. "For me, this is a foot-in-the-door technique, and a gateway into game dev," he continues. "You can see, and you can learn how things are made, how things can be built. We actually hired so many modders. I would say, at this point, half of the quest team is all former modders."
While this isn’t a completely new revelation as far as CDPR is concerned (Sasko actually revealed this information back in 2024), it certainly couldn’t come at a funnier time, given the ongoing discussion around the differing sentiments toward community patches, mods, and emulation happening between Western players and Japanese fans on social media right now.
It’s an exciting era for Cyberpunk chooms; Edgerunners 2 just released on Netflix to rave reviews, alongside a host of new additions to the actual game, which include a dual-wielding playstyle, fresh cyberware customization options, and even a mode that gives you a tour through Night City, on top of cute references to the anime spinoff.
You can read our review for Edgerunners 2 here, as well as our interviews with producer Bartozs Szytbor, who told us all about Roman’s backstory and why the show’s ending wasn’t what audiences anticipated.
Returning to Cyberpunk 2077 or playing it for the first time? We’ve got a new and improved Cyberpunk interactive map to help you find every mission, Iconic item, and collectible in the game. Plus, we’ve also got a full walkthrough for the base game, a Phantom Liberty walkthrough, and an overview of all the Cyberpunk 2077 endings so you don’t make a choice you regret. And we can’t ignore the various romance options you can smooch, which also impact how V’s story concludes.

item.title: Annie Potts, who portrayed a younger version of Sheldon’s Meemaw on Young Sheldon, revealed how she felt about the show’s finale, disagreeing with how adult Sheldon remained "mean and unchanged" in Parsons' finale cameo.
item.description:
Annie Potts, who portrayed a younger version of Sheldon’s Meemaw on Young Sheldon, revealed how she felt about the show’s finale, disagreeing with how adult Sheldon remained "mean and unchanged" in Parsons' finale cameo.
The end of Young Sheldon — the seven-season-long Big Bang Theory Spinoff show — was rife with drama. Its abrupt ending was reportedly revealed to cast members in a Zoom call, with Potts saying she felt “blindsided” by the decision and went "full Meemaw” on the series’ producers.
She elaborated on these feelings in a book authored by Jessica Radloff titled Young Sheldon: The (Juicier-Than-Meemaw’s-Brisket) Inside Story of the Hit Comedy, where she described her reaction to Jim Parson’s cameo at the end of the final episode as a grown-up Sheldon.
According to Radloff’s book, Potts was “a little sad” about how Sheldon remained “mean and unchanged” as a character despite all the events of the prequel series.
“That broke my heart,” she told the author. “It was like, ‘Really? Still no responsibility?’ It was just selfishness. It’s just not how I wish to see Sheldon off into the world. …I thought the show could have ended [with young Sheldon] and not to the dreaded scene with Jim and Mayim as Sheldon and Amy revealing he was unchanged and unrepentant. That gave me a stomachache. It was like, ‘Who crashed our party?! Who invited you?'”
While most of the cast reportedly felt similarly burnt by the situation, Young Sheldon himself, Iain Armitage, said he was probably the only member who was actually happy that the show was finally over.
“Looking back now, it’s nostalgic-sad,” he said. “Like, I miss working at Warner Bros., I miss the crew and the people I love. I love the act of acting. I love doing it. It’s fun. But not really specific moments. More the overall thing.”
He went on to call the intense reaction to the show’s cancellation from his fellow castmates as “heavy and annoying and weird,” saying he wanted to be back in Virginia.
“I wanted to be traveling, and I’m happy to do whatever movie comes up. And my mom has always imbued me with a very healthy sense of ephemerality, and the fact that nothing good can last and everything changes, and that’s a good thing,” he continued. “I would hate to be on a show playing 23-year-old Sheldon. That would suck. I wouldn’t want to do that. So it was a perfect time to end it,” he said in the book.
A Young Sheldon spinoff series was greenlit (news that, reportedly, also blindsided the original show’s cast), focusing on Georgie and Mandy as young parents in the 90s. It was first announced in 2024 and is still running today, currently on its third season.

item.title: Tom Skerritt, the rugged, mustachioed actor best known to IGN readers for his roles in Top Gun and Alien, passed away from natural causes on Wednesday at the age of 93.
item.description:
Tom Skerritt, the rugged, mustachioed actor best known to IGN readers for his roles in Top Gun and Alien, passed away from natural causes on Wednesday at the age of 93.
“We are heartbroken by his loss,” Skerritt’s family said in a statement provided to The Hollywood Reporter.
“While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity and the love he brought into our lives. He cared deeply about imagination, creativity, storytelling, service, veterans, the natural world and helping others find and share their own voices.”
Skerritt first gained acclaim as a film actor in director Robert Altman’s 1970 comedy M*A*S*H, where he played surgeon Duke Forrest, one of the few characters not included in the later classic TV series adaptation.
Other notable films of Skerritt’s in the 1970s include Harold and Maude, The Turning Point, Fuzz, Thieves Like Us, and Cheech & Chong’s Up in Smoke.
After initially turning down the role, Skerritt played Captain Arthur Dallas in Ridley Scott’s now classic sci-fi/horror film Alien (1979). Skerritt belonged to an ensemble that included Sigourney Weaver, Yaphet Kotto, Ian Holm, John Hurt, Harry Dean Stanton, and Veronica Cartwright. (Be sure to read Scott Collura's deep-dive interview with Tom Skerritt about the making of Alien.)
During the 1980s, Skerritt had roles in films such as The Dead Zone, Wisdom, SpaceCamp, Poltergeist III, and Steel Magnolias. But the role from that decade Skerritt best came to be remembered for is Commander Mike "Viper" Metcalf in 1986’s Top Gun. As the Commanding Officer of the Top Gun program, Viper had to keep hot shot US Navy fighter pilots like Tom Cruise’s Maverick and Val Kilmer’s Iceman in check.
Skerritt’s most notable film role in the 1990s was as the father of Brad Pitt and Craig Sheffer’s character in director Robert Redford’s 1992 drama A River Runs Through It.
He later appeared in Singles, Contact, Smoke Signals, Tears of the Sun, Whiteout, and A Hologram for the King. Skerritt played himself in Seth McFarlane’s 2012 comedy Ted.
While Skerritt’s career in television goes back to the early 1960s, his most notable role on the screen was as Sheriff Jimmy Brock in the David E. Kelley-created 1992-96 series Picket Fences. Skerritt won a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for the role. The actor also did stints on Cheers, Brothers & Sisters, Huff, and The Good Wife.
Born Thomas Roy Skerritt on August 25, 1933 in Detroit, Michigan, Skerritt was married three times and had five children. He was also a military veteran having served in the US Air Force from 1951-55.

item.title: Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival has been a smash hit, says Saber Interactive CEO Matthew Karch in a post on LinkedIn, and it’s the first of a "series" of releases from the studio that will improve its methodology.
item.description:
Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival has been a smash hit, says Saber Interactive CEO Matthew Karch in a post on LinkedIn, and it’s the first of a “series” of releases from the studio that will improve how it makes games in the future.
Hellraiser: Revival has proven to be a smashing success, in spite of — or, perhaps because of — its super-spicy content. The game doesn’t skirt around the sex, blood, and gore that defined the source material, causing some content creators to get permanently banned despite taking pains to censor their playthroughs.
In an October 19 LinkedIn post, Saber Interactive CEO Matthew Karch praised the Hellraiser development team, revealing the title has been performing “extremely well on PC and console” since its October 8 release.
He also speculated that AAA titles with massive budgets and lengthy development timelines won’t be sustainable in the industry for much longer (if, indeed, they are right now), instead positing that AA games based on established IPs with smaller budgets are likely a more realistic path forward.
“The game is testament to the notion that an established IP and solid AA development with controlled costs can produce great results and high user scores,” he wrote. “I believe a greater focus on these middle-market IP-driven products, rather than AAA behemoths, is the future to maintaining growth and momentum in the game industry.
“While I believe there will always be a place for the properly-developed and budgeted AAA experience, a AA game that provides a great immersive experience for a lower price is less risky and can provide much greater returns on average.”
Karch went on to say that Hellraiser: Revival is “the first in a series of releases by Saber that will continue to prove out our methodology,” teasing that there’s “more to come in just a few short weeks.”
While IGN scored the game a six out of ten, Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival boasts a “very positive” player score on Steam, and has earned no small amount of praise from content creators who showed up in droves to broadcast the game on release.
Of course, given its content, it’s no surprise that some streamers got the ban hammer — but, according to its developers, that’s exactly what they were aiming for when they made it.
"It was an unofficial goal of the team to be banned, unrated, or restricted at least somewhere in the world as one barometer of whether we’d done our jobs right,” narrative director Antony De Fault told IGN in an exclusive interview.
Even Clive Barker himself was impressed, saying he was “fearful at one point that the game would be overly censored but I’m genuinely astonished by how far they’ve been able to push it.”

item.title: Prime Video has officially renewed Mike Flanagan’s Carrie for a second season, saying there’s “much more in store” for our favorite prom queen.
item.description:
Prime Video has officially renewed Mike Flanagan’s Carrie for a second season, saying there’s “much more in store” for our favorite prom queen.
Amazon announced the news today, October 22, revealing that Carrie skyrocketed to the number one spot on Prime Video across 105 countries worldwide. It’s no surprise; the show was well-received by critics and audiences alike, sparking no end of fan theories and comparisons to other adaptations of Stephen King’s debut novel.
As per a press release from Prime Video, Carrie’s story is “far from over,” and “much remains in store from Mike Flanagan and Stephen King, as new revelations will come to light, major character arcs, and plenty of shocking twists.”
"Carrie is connecting with both longtime Stephen King fans and a new generation altogether — including young adults and international audiences, with particular strength among female viewers," Amazon MGM Studios’ Head of Global Television, Peter Friedlander, said in a statement. "It speaks to the enduring power of this story and signals that Mike Flanagan's reimagining of the iconic IP has real breadth. We're excited by where he and Stephen plan to take the story."
Mike Flanagan also shared excitement to continue Carrie’s story past the original novel. “For 50 years, audiences have known and gravitated to Carrie White’s story. From the beginning, we imagined a story that goes far beyond the prom, and I’m incredibly grateful for Stephen’s trust and support in exploring what comes next,” he said.
“I can’t wait for audiences to get to see what’s down the road for Carrie White. Mike Flanagan and I are excited about what comes next. It’s bound to be thrilling,” Stephen King, who served as executive producer on the show, added.
Warning: Spoilers for Carrie ahead!
Flanagan’s Carrie was always ripe for a second season. It notably included elements from King’s other works like The Dark Tower and Doctor Sleep, and perhaps most importantly, Carrie lives at the end, being whisked away to safety by astral projector Emaline as they flee from Adelaide and a shadowy group of fellow telekinetics with the Shine.
There’s much we don’t know about this growing storyline, and although it deviates wildly from King’s original novel, it’s being produced by the man himself, who has expressed nothing but positivity for Flanagan’s take on the source material and is clearly jazzed for a second season.
Carrie offers a modern-day retelling of the ‘74 book that resonates with 2026 viewers, portraying the harsh realities of being a student in an increasingly dangerous learning environment, current political issues, and the real impact social media has on peoples’ lives.
Carrie is available to watch on Prime Video right now. IGN scored the show an eight out of ten, with reviewer Tom Jorgensen saying: “With smart story accommodations for the social media age and a pair of stellar performances from Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan, Mike Flanagan and his team have successfully made the case for why Carrie’s story needed to be retold.”

item.title: In a recent interview with GameSpot, actor Debra Wilson, who you might recognize from Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order, Wolfenstein: The New Colossus, or God of War Ragnarok, said she’s sick of seeing her face in video games. The actor said the developers choose it and she’d rather play characters that don’t resemble her.
item.description:
In a recent interview with GameSpot, actor Debra Wilson, who you might recognize from Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order, Wolfenstein: The New Colossus, or God of War Ragnarok, said she’s sick of seeing her face in video games. The actor said the developers choose it and she’d rather play characters that don’t resemble her.
“I don’t necessarily dig it,” Wilson said. “Because I might as well be doing it on camera. It's hard to suspend your disbelief. There are people who are like, ‘Oh my God, she's in every f***ing game. What the f***?’ And there are other people like, ‘I am sick of looking at her face because I just want to play the game and not think of Debra Wilson.’”
It’s become a bit of a meme in gaming communities, with players complaining that they’re being taken out of the experience because they’ve seen Wilson’s face pop up.
“I don't blame them because I feel the same,” she said. “Why do you have to show my face? Amanda Waller in Suicide Squad, Grace Walker in Wolfenstein: The New Colossus, and now with the new Wolverine game coming out, I'm Callisto. Guess who the f*** she looks like?
“They wanted to scan my original tattoos. I was like, ‘Now you're pushing it. No, you're pushing that s**t.’ So I have been grateful for the work that has come in the video game industry where my characters are European.”
Later in the interview, she talked about how she wouldn’t want to include it as a contract stipulation because she wants artists to be able to tell stories in whatever way they like. But as an actor who’s played demons, dragons, and all sorts of other non-human entities, it doesn’t really capture what she’s capable of.
She also noted that it depends on the game. In Death Stranding 2, her likeness was used but so was almost every other actor’s.
“I am not upset at their choice to do that because everybody looks like themselves,” she said. “[Hideo Kojima] knew what he wanted. He's more than a director. He's an artist.”
Wilson recently starred as Jessica Pike in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, Callisto in Marvel’s Wolverine, and did background voices in Modern Warfare 4.

item.title: Speaking on the Kyle Buchanan Show, Inde Navarrette gave her impression of Gen Z’s renewed interest in going to the movies and what kinds of pictures they’re keen on seeing following the success of Backrooms and Obsession over the summer.
item.description:
Speaking on the Kyle Buchanan Show, Inde Navarrette gave her impression of Gen Z’s renewed interest in going to the movies and what kinds of pictures they’re keen on seeing, following the success of Backrooms and Obsession over the summer.
It’s safe to say that Inde Navarrette has a bright future ahead of her, in no small part due to her standout performance in Curry Barker’s Obsession. The movie quickly became one of the most profitable indie flicks ever made and brought oodles of younger viewers to theaters, earning rave reviews from audiences and critics alike.
This, alongside the success of 21-year-old Kane Parson’s Backrooms, have highlighted a growing trend among moviegoers; young audiences are keen on seeing original stories brought to the screen and love when studios take a chance on new talent.
Navarrette echoed this sentiment during her interview on the Kyle Buchanan Show, where the host asked her what Gen Z wants to see on the silver screen.
“I think Gen Z just wants to go to something that they don’t feel like they’re being sold,” she answered. “I think that maybe we are tired constantly of having ads in movies or production placement and all of these things. We understand it’s fundamental, right? We grew up with commercials that are fun that we still quote, like State Farm and Aflac, or whatever. It’s kind of fun. But we don’t want to be sold. We want original stories.”
“Just because we’re living in the time of technology doesn’t mean we’re not living a human life or feeling human experiences. I’m happy Obsession brought that to the table. We want originality and authenticity, and we want to feel,” she continued.
Navarrette’s remarks speak to the rise in popularity for horror films and smaller projects lately. In fact, Backrooms kicked off an industry-wide rush to snatch up the rights to internet copypasta IPs to greenlight films for the likes of The Mandela Catalogue (directed by Spielberg, himself), The SCP Foundation, and even Siren Head, with none other than Zach Cregger onboard to produce.
The Obsession actress isn’t wrong; as pointed out by Variety, a study from Fandango found that Gen Z is the largest demographic of moviegoers right now, with 87% — alongside 82% of millennials — going to theaters to see at least one movie over the last year.
Fandango executive vice president Jerramy Hainline remarked on this data, saying, “While there has been a perception that Gen Z is less engaged with theatrical moviegoing, our data shows that their momentum has been building. What’s especially notable is how strongly they value the shared, communal aspect of the experience, reinforcing that theaters continue to play an important role as a social destination for younger audiences.”
Navarrette is now pivoting toward a much larger project, having been confirmed to play Rogue in Marvel’s X-Men reboot. She’s also keen on voicing a character in a Resident Evil game, and said she studied anime like Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer to better understand scriptwriting and storytelling.

item.title: A Valve developer mistakenly slipped up and made mention of Half-Life 3's long rumored codename during a recent conference.
item.description:
A Valve developer mistakenly slipped up and made mention of Half-Life 3's long-rumored codename during a recent conference.
For years, fans have wondered if we'll ever see Half-Life 3. During the 2010s, hope for the threequel was kept firmly alive by die-hard fans... but it was later revealed that the project had been quietly killed by Valve. However, hope was reignited when Valve released Half-Life: Alyx, which ended with a massive cliffhanger that seemed to directly set up Gordon Freeman's next adventure. Ever since then, there have been rumors of a third game, with various dataminers discovering references to a project known as "HLX" in various Valve-related files. It has been believed for years that HLX is indeed Half-Life 3, as no one has been able to link it to any other existing Valve project. (And, of course, the acronym all but screaming that it's Half-Life related.)
Now, Valve has acknowleged the project itself, though not on purpose. During a recent Q&A panel at GameSoundCon, a conference for video game audio, Valve's music designer, Mike Morasky, was explaining how the developer handled certain sound systems and noted that Deadlock uses a particular type of high dynamic range audio... and HLX uses its own kind of HDR.
We have the first mention of HLX by a Valve employee.HLX files today. I'm working as quickly as I can. https://t.co/LhFBNOP1CU
Once the words HLX came out of Morasky's mouth, he pretty much stopped talking. Whether that's because he had finished his thought or if he realized he should stop talking is up in the air. A colleague sitting next to Morasky then quietly said "nice work," which some fans have read into as a passive-agressive retort to Morasky's slip up. Fans went buckwild with this small, but notable mistake. Some ran with it, feeling like all of their theories and copium has been vindicated after this mention.
Regardless, this does seem to confirm that HLX is a project that is still actively in development at Valve. We can only hope that it is the long-rumored Half-Life 3, but who knows how far away it could be from being announced, let alone released. Half-Life: Alyx had an exceptionally fast turn around time for being announced and released, so it's possible that a similar pattern would emerge here. If that's the case, maybe we can hope to see it at The Game Awards, but that's still probably a longshot.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Seth Rogen, Brad Bird, and Travis Knight will showcase upcoming animated projects like Tangles and Wildwood at L.A.’s Infinity Festival this November.
item.description:
Seth Rogen, Brad Bird, and more are headed to next month’s Infinity Festival in Los Angeles. The event, which explores “the intersection of Hollywood, Silicon Valley and emerging technologies through programming spanning film, television, gaming, animation, music, and more” is slated to showcase how technology is transforming storytelling.
This year's lineup features the team behind the animated film Tangles, including Rogen, who’s producing and voice acting in the movie, along with producer Lauren Miller Rogen, director, producer, and co-screenwriter Leah Nelson, and co-writer Sarah Leavitt. A special screening of Tangles will also be shown at the festival.
Additionally, The Incredibles and Ratatouille filmmaker Brad Bird will be honored with Infinity Festival's Lifetime Achievement Award for his contributions to animation and filmmaking. Bird is directing the upcoming Netflix/Skydance animated feature Ray Gunn, which will receive a special screening at Infinity Festival.
Finally, Travis Knight, President and CEO of LAIKA and director of the studio's upcoming stop-motion animated feature Wildwood will be presented with Infinity Festival's Monolith Award for Visionary Storytelling, recognizing “his innovative approach to animation and filmmaking.” As part of the Infinity Festival, Knight will offer an “inside look at the creative process behind Wildwood, including the groundbreaking technologies developed specifically to bring the film to life.”The Infinity Festival is slated to take place November 12-15 in Los Angeles. For more information about the Infinity Festival, check out www.infinityfestival.com.

item.title: A trailer for Mass Effect 5 meant for internal purposes at BioWare has leaked online, offering a glimpse at what might have been.
item.description:
A trailer for Mass Effect 5 meant for internal purposes at BioWare has leaked online, offering a glimpse at what might have been.
The trailer, which IGN has verified as legitimate, was created for EA leadership last year and was not meant for the public. It appeared on Reddit just a day after EA's shock cancelation of Mass Effect 5 and the closure of its developer, BioWare.
The trailer begins with a message, "The following is in-engine footage from our small team. It uses our pre-production assets," and ends with the title 'Mass Effect: Universe.' It is unclear if this is would have been the final name of the game.
The trailer has a number of familiar elements, including weaponry, powers, and alien species we've seen in previous Mass Effect games. There's a glimpse at a sex scene, a Mass Effect relay, space travel, and a nightclub, all of which are Mass Effect staples. There's even a galaxy map on display inside your ship.
It looks like players would have assumed the role of a former military operative now in a "new line of work." Their job is to stop fires before they start, we're told. An older Liara T'Soni appears, helping the player character out in a bar fight.
BioWare had spent the past half decade teasing the next Mass Effect's setting and story, so we know a little of what the developer was planning to do with the game. We'd had it confirmed that Mass Effect 5 would have been set hundreds of years after Mass Effect 3, and feature a narrative that re-centers the action on the franchise's original Milky Way setting, long after the Reapers were defeated.
Liara's return had already been teased long before this trailer emerged. We also knew the geth would have returned alongside some Andromeda races, suggesting contact had been made with the colonists that travelled there. Romance was (of course) set to make a return, as was the Paragon/Renegade system.
Since yesterday’s dramatic news, a number of people who had worked on Mass Effect 5 talked in vague terms about the game it was shaping up to be. On X / Twitter, New York Times bestselling author Catherynne M. Valente responded to a user who said, “A game industry that cannot figure out how to make a sequel to the literal best game of all time is a game industry that is fundamentally broken,” with: “We did figure it out. We were working on a great game. Just saying.”
One person who was laid off from BioWare, cinematic supervisor Tony de Waal, took to LinkedIn to say Mass Effect 5 would have been “something special,” offering players “a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match.”
“We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy,” he continued.
“I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking, and sad for the small, talented group of devs who were all punching above their weight to make something special. Please consider those who stayed with BioWare until the very end. They are truly some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career.”
Earlier today, IGN reported that a public-facing Mass Effect 5 trailer was ready to go before EA canceled the game and shut BioWare down. This was first mentioned in a post on the subreddit for Austin, Texas, where BioWare had a studio. An alleged EA worker spoke of “a trailer ready for Mass Effect 5 that I saw a few months ago, so I’m puzzled as to how ‘early’ they were.”
This is in reference to EA’s solitary paragraph on BioWare’s closure and the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 in the memo Cam Weber, president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, president and COO, sent to staff on Wednesday:
“As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly.”
The mention of the next Mass Effect being in “early development” shocked some fans, given it was announced at The Game Awards in December 2020. At the time, BioWare said the project was in “early production.”
According to Bloomberg, BioWare had around 50 staff working on Mass Effect 5 when EA closed it down. The decision comes two years after 2024’s launch of Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet EA’s sales expectations. It wasn't long after The Veilguard came out that EA gutted the studio. Now, this latest round of layoffs will see 400 jobs reportedly axed across EA, amounting to 3% of total staff. BioWare’s Austin studio reportedly remains open, working to support various EA games in development. IGN has asked EA for comment.
The end of Mass Effect and BioWare comes just weeks before the annual N7 Day, set for November 7. Less than 12 months ago, Mike Gamble, executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, celebrated N7 Day to say the next Mass Effect game was still in development, to express excitement about the Amazon TV series (which IGN understands is currently still in the works), and to insist EA and BioWare "remain committed to telling more stories in this universe."
Fans had hoped to see more of Mass Effect 5 on N7 Day next month, but it now seems likely to pass without fanfare. “You made me laugh. Thank you,” Gamble replied to one X / Twitter user who wondered what might be announced on N7 Day.
We have much more on the dramatic news of BioWare's closure, including reaction from fans and the video game industry, IGN's Ryan McCaffrey on why BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever, and the thoughts of one former BioWare developer on the possibility of Dragon Age and Mass Effect living on.

item.title: The New York Game Awards is officially returning for its 16th show at the SVA Theatre in Manhattan on January 19, 2027, and IGN will be streaming the whole thing on our website and YouTube channels.
item.description:
The New York Video Game Critics Circle (NYVGCC) has announced that The New York Game Awards is officially returning for its 16th show at the SVA Theatre in Manhattan on January 19, 2027, and IGN will be streaming the whole thing on our website and YouTube channels.
The 2027 New York Game Awards will be hosted by gaming and tech content creator Lara Lunardi and TV personality and former ESPN anchor Arda Ocal, and NYVGCC co-founder and president Harold Goldberg, former Nintendo president Reggie Fils-Aimé, and NYVGCC executive dirrector Ryan O'Callaghan will also be in attendance.
If you wish to see the awards show in person, you can buy tickets through Humanitix for $85, and there will also be a limited number of $100 VIP tickets that will get you preferred seating and access to the after-party presented by New Blood Interactive.
Proceeds from the New York Game Awards support NYVGCC's Playing with Purpose writing program, which "brings comprehensive classes and workshops in journalism and game narrative writing to schools and shelters across New York City."
“The New York Game Awards is our way of paying homage to our New York roots while recognizing the heart and soul of our industry by spotlighting game studios of all sizes,” Goldberg said. “We have a really great lineup this year, and we’re incredibly grateful to have Lara and Arda join us to host our awards show. We know their energy will bring a great dynamic to our yearly festivities.”
More details about the upcoming New York Game Awards show will be released at a future date, including who will be the Andrew Yoon Legend Award recipient and info on a surprise post-awards musical performance.

item.title: Dispatch is now officially one year old! To celebrate, Adhoc is giving fans oodles of new content in the form of a commentary track and storyboard modes, a new mobile version of the game, a live concert with a performance from Prism herself, and yes, more merch.
item.description:
Dispatch is now officially one year old! To celebrate, AdHoc Studio is giving fans oodles of new content in the form of a commentary track and storyboard modes, a new mobile version of the game, a live concert with a performance from Prism herself, and yes, more merch.
AdHoc’s debut title, Dispatch, released to rave reviews on October 22, 2025. Made up of Telltale alumni, the devs truly flexed their storytelling chops with this game, bringing players along for Robert’s journey from zero to hero alongside a chaotic cast of lovable, super-powered characters.
A year later, fans are anxiously awaiting more updates on AdHoc’s next project — but in the meantime, they can whet their appetites on some exciting additions to Dispatch and fun experiences that bring the game's digital world to reality.
Now included in Dispatch's Deluxe Edition are a Commentary Mode and Storyboard Mode. Commentary Mode brings players back to the days of DVD Special Features with two separate audio tracks, where the game’s actors and developers chat about the project in the background as the game progresses. Each choice will give you new insights into the game, so there’s even more replayability for curious fans who want all the gritty details about how Dispatch was made. Storyboard mode shows players the sketches that laid out how the game's scenes were planned, and it can even be paired with Commentary Mode for a double-whammy.
The Deluxe Edition also comes with a digital art book and four digital comics. What’s more, those who already own the Deluxe Edition will get the Commentary and Storyboard modes for free, while those who have the standard version of the game can upgrade for $10.99 USD.
But wait, there’s more! Dispatch is also coming to mobile, letting you join Rob on his adventures wherever you’re at in the world. The game releases on Android and iOS on December 9, 2026, with additional support for Google Play Games on PC. The base game has been rebuilt for touch screens and vertical play, and mobile players can get the first four episodes for free. The full release will cost $19.99, with pre-orders opening on the Google Play store and Apple store soon.
Fans have been begging for more merchandise in the months since Dispatch first came to Steam, and now, they finally get their wish. A three-record soundtrack vinyl set, featuring artwork from Dispatch’s art director, Derek Stratton, will be available to purchase, and 100 of those will be signed by him. Shirts, hoodies, and four physical comics are also available for purchase, with each volume boasting an individual cover that creates an epic battle scene when placed side by side. A Dispatch: Design Works hardcover book and collectible box are also up for sale, going behind the scenes with concept art, cast interviews, developer insights, and more. And for the real collectors out there, the first 1,000 orders placed on the official online store will get a never-before-seen limited edition, numbered collector’s card.
Perhaps most excitingly, the music of Dispatch is getting brought to life with a special concert for one night only. On Thursday, December 3, fans can gather at the AVALON Hollywood to watch ‘Hoes Depressed’ singer and the voice of Prism, THOT SQUAD, perform songs from the game live alongside Bershy, Primer, Caroline Kingsbury, and Fartbarf. Tickets for this event are extremely limited, with AdHoc Studio email subscribers getting first pick before they open up to the general public. It's an in-person event only, so it won't be streamed, and you'll want to get your tickets fast.
"Dispatch was only possible because of folks who believed in it enough to show up and do their best work. In our industry, it's often really hard to showcase those people and how the development process actually works, but fortunately our game is very weird and specific and affords us some unique opportunities." said Nick Herman, Co-Creative Director on Dispatch and COO of AdHoc Studio.
"So for the fans who made Dispatch a part of their lives, we wanted to give them more ways to experience the world they love, whether that’s playing alongside the cast and crew, experiencing the entire game in its original storyboards, or hanging out together IRL at the wildest version of a Dispatch concert our finance team would sign off on."
If you haven't gotten to play Dispatch yet, now is the time. IGN scored the game a glowing 9 out of 10, with reviewer Sara Thwaites calling it a "sharp-witted workplace comedy that charms with its smart dialogue choices, great writing, and lovably aggravating cast."
